what_this_is: The Workshop rows for pulling a person's messages and saved items from the services they use and answering them, one row per service, all running one mechanism in tools/pull-from-connected-accounts; plus one row that reads back what an earlier version kept (it has nothing to read once pulls keep nothing). A service is one JSON description in read-data/sources/; the person's token reaches the one process on a private pipe and is never in the request.

payload.label: Pull the messages from the Discord text channels my bot can read
payload.job: Pull the messages from the Discord text channels my bot can read and hand them back
payload.description: Reads the text and announcement channels of every server the bot is in (only those the bot may view and read the history of), newest messages first, and answers them folded into held: a message pulled twice appears once, an edited message replaces the older copy, and a renamed channel takes its new title. The bot cannot read anyone's personal direct messages, and a message's text is empty unless the bot has the Message Content setting. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Discord bot token (name discord-bot-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Discord did not accept the token; unreachable), the conversations (threads) and saved items (collections) that are new or changed, each exactly as the service sent them, how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor to hand back as held.cursor, and any failed requests in errors. It keeps nothing: hand in held (what earlier pulls answered) to fold into it, and keep the answer where you keep such things.

account.description: A name that tells this account from your other accounts on the same service (for example work). Default: default.

limit.description: How many messages or items to ask for in one request.

most_pages.description: How many pages of one conversation or list to read.

most_threads.description: At most this many conversations are read in one pull.

held.description: What earlier pulls of this account answered, kept by the caller: { cursor?, threads: [{ id, title, messages, source? }], collections: { name: [item] } }. The pull folds what it reads into it, stops paging at what it already holds, and starts from its cursor. Left out, everything the walk reaches is new.

threads.description: The conversations that are new or changed, each whole: { id, title, messages (exactly as the service sent them, oldest first), source? }

collections.description: The saved items that are new or changed, by collection name, exactly as the service sent them

cursor.description: Hand back as held.cursor next time

payload.label: Pull the Signal conversations my client printed
payload.job: Pull the Signal conversations my client printed and hand them back
payload.description: Answers the conversations a Signal client on your computer printed (signal-cli output, handed in as conversations) as conversations, folded into held, with who the account is (self_id). It asks no one and holds no token: the Signal client holds its own login and the transport that runs it is a different row. A message pulled twice appears once, an edit replaces the older copy, messages stay exactly as printed in time order, and the cursor is the greatest message time seen, which the transport asks the client from next time. Give self_id and conversations, and optionally account (a name for this account, default "default"), held and most_threads. Answers status (pulled), the conversations that are new or changed (threads), how many new messages arrived, the cursor to hand back as held.cursor, and anything that failed in errors. It keeps nothing.

self_id.description: The identity Signal knows this account by. A message from it is the account's own.

conversations.description: What the person's Signal client printed: a list of conversations, each { id, name?, type?, messages: [{ id?, timestamp (epoch milliseconds), from, body?, editedTimestamp?, type? }] }.

The pull folds what it reads into it, stops paging at what it already holds, and starts from its cursor. Left out, everything the walk reaches is new.

payload.label: Read my Signal messages on this computer
payload.job: Read my Signal messages on this computer
payload.description: Runs the Signal client (signal-cli) on your computer, which reads the messages Signal holds for this computer as a linked device, turns them into conversations (a group by its name, a person by the name their messages came with; your own messages sent from your phone are yours) and answers them the way tool:pull-my-signal-messages does, folded into held: a message read twice appears once, an edit replaces the older copy, calls stay calls, and receipts, typing, reactions and group changes are left out and counted. The computer fetches signal-cli and the Java it needs itself, the first time, from their publishers, checked against pinned hashes; nothing is installed and you do nothing. It must be linked once first (tool:link-signal-on-this-computer); until then it answers needs_link and starts nothing. Signal hands each message to a linked device once, so what arrived is written down on this computer before it is answered and handed in again if the run failed before answering. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), timeout_seconds (how long to wait for messages, default 5), most_messages, most_threads and held, all optional. It keeps nothing.

account.description: A name that tells this account from your other Signal accounts (for example work). Default: default.

most_messages.description: At most this many messages are read in one run. Default 1000.

most_threads.description: At most this many conversations are kept in one run.

held.description: What earlier pulls of this account answered, kept by the caller: { cursor?, threads: [{ id, title, messages, source? }], collections: { name: [item] } }. The pull folds what it reads into it, stops paging at what it already holds, and starts from its cursor. Left out, everything the walk reaches is new.

payload.label: Link Signal on this computer
payload.job: Link my Signal account to this computer so my messages can be read here
payload.description: Links this computer to your Signal account as one of its devices, once, so tool:read-my-signal-messages-on-this-computer can read your messages here. The computer fetches signal-cli and the Java it needs itself. It runs as a session: as soon as Signal gives the link it prints { state: "scan", link, qr_text, qr_svg }, the code to scan, and keeps waiting; on your phone open Signal, Settings, Linked devices, Link new device, and scan it. It then answers { state: "linked", self_id }, or not_linked with why (a code is good for about a minute: run it again for a new one). Signal's keys for this device stay in a folder on this computer that only this tool's runs are given. Already linked, it answers linked and asks nothing.

linux-aarch64.unverified: signal-cli 0.14.9's libsignal-client 0.103.0 jar holds no linux aarch64 library (it holds macOS aarch64 and x86_64, linux x86_64 and Windows x86_64), so the client cannot start there.

provenance.source: signal-cli's own `link` command; the QR code is drawn with uqr
